questions.nlq: Hey! I noticed some events had tons of people—specifically, those with more than 5 members attending. Once we narrow it down to those popular ones, what's the average amount spent on food for all of them?

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I mean the single average value calculated from all the food spending records for those events combined, just one number for the whole group.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT AVG(e.cost) AS avg_food_spent
FROM expense e
JOIN budget b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id
WHERE b.category = 'Food'
AND b.link_to_event IN (
    SELECT link_to_event
    FROM attendance
    GROUP BY link_to_event
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 5
)

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I want the average amount spent on food calculated separately for each of those popular events, so I can see them listed out by event.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT b.spent
FROM event e
JOIN attendance a ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event
JOIN budget b ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event
WHERE b.category = 'Food'
GROUP BY e.event_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) > 5

SELECT SUM(e.cost) AS total_spent_on_food
FROM "expense" e
JOIN "budget" b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id
JOIN "member" m ON e.link_to_member = m.member_id
WHERE b.category = 'Food'
  AND m.link_to_major IS NOT NULL;

WITH qualified AS (

    JOIN "attendance" a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id

    INTERSECT
    SELECT b.link_to_event
    FROM "budget" b
    WHERE b.category = 'Food' AND b.spent > 100
)

    HAVING COUNT(*) > 5

    FROM "budget" b
    WHERE b.category = 'Food' AND b.spent > 100
)
SELECT SUM(b.amount) AS total_budget
FROM "budget" b
